articles.title: Who Keeps the Skill: A Randomized Trial of AI Patent Drafting at Eleven Firms
articles.content:
一项最新的NBER工作论文公布了在实践专利律师中进行的AI辅助控制试验的结果。主要发现如下：

1. 使用AI工具（谷歌内部的InFlow工具）的律师起草了更好的专利申请；且随着使用时间的增长（10天与90天的使用对比），申请质量有所提升。（由外部律所的盲测专利律师根据可执行性、技术准确性、战略模糊性、完整性和清晰度等标准评分）

2. 大部分改进体现在避免低质量工作，而非达到最高水平。同时，初级律师的工作通过AI获得的改进比资深律师更明显（资深律师本身已处于较高水准）

3. 使用AI后，资深律师在没有AI辅助的情况下（如编辑草稿）的某些任务也表现得更好

4. 使用AI后，初级律师在没有AI辅助的情况下工作表现平均未见改善，但部分人显著提升而其他人则明显退步

研究结论明确，AI在专利行业中扮演着重要角色。我持续思考的问题是：如何利用AI同时仍能发展律师（和人类）的技能？

参考文献：
David Autor等人，《AI辅助是否增强还是削弱专业能力？来自三个月专利起草现场实验的证据》，NBER工作论文第35720号（2026年9月）
articles.summary:
by Dennis Crouch

A new NBER working paper reports results of a controlled trial of AI assistance among practicing patent attorneys. Findings:

  1. Lawyers using the AI tool (Google's internal InFlow tool) drafted better applications; and the applications improved over time (10 days vs 90 days of use). (Blinded patent attorneys at an outside firm scored submissions on enforceability, technical accuracy, strategic ambiguity, completeness, and clarity).
  2. Most of the improvement was in avoiding awful work, rather than achieving the highest quality. Along with this, the work of junior attorneys saw more improvement with AI than did experienced attorneys (who were already operating at a higher level).
  3. After using AI, experienced attorneys were also better at certain tasks (editing a draft) without AI.
  4. After using AI, junior attorneys (on average) saw no improvement in their skills without AI. But some saw significant skill gain and others saw significant skill reduction.

The outcome here is clear that AI has an important role in the patent business and the question I keep thinking about is how to use AI while still building skill as an attorney (and human).

David Autor et al., Does AI Assistance Enhance or Erode Expertise? Evidence from a Three-Month Field Experiment in Patent Drafting, NBER Working Paper No. 35720 (Sept. 2026).

articles.title: Back to Vail: The IP CLE Conference, January 6-9, 2027
articles.content:
2027年1月6日至9日，知识产权持续教育（IP CLE）会议将再次返回科罗拉多州韦尔镇的大茂雅特酒店举行。我将继续负责周六上午的专利案例法回顾。该会议由大律师事务所Debevoise & Plimpton的合伙人大卫·伯恩斯坦（David Bernstein）和Michael Best律师事务所的斯科特·阿尔特（Scott Alter）共同主办，并由美国律师协会（ABA）知识产权法分会联合赞助。

这个会议以滑雪为特色，日程安排围绕山景进行：上午的会议从7:00开始，持续到9:15，中午是休会“滑雪时间”，下午4:00到7:00恢复会议。

我已经连续多年参加这个会议，吸引我的不仅是参会人员的多样性，还有山景的冬季风光。美国联邦巡回法院法官卡拉·斯托尔（Kara Stoll）和东德克萨斯州联邦地区法院法官J.坎贝尔·巴克（J. Campbell Barker）将在周六下午闭幕式上与威利·杰伊（Willy Jay）进行法官与律师的对话。威利·杰伊是一位在最高法院和上诉法院实践的律师，上个月加入了Paul Weiss律师事务所。

周五和周六有两场企业内部律师小组讨论：周五由CoorsTek、Sandisk和Medtronic律师参与；周六则有Dolby、Samsung、Microsoft、Pure Storage和Intel律师参与。

**专利议程**
周六上午是专利密集部分：Baker Botts律师事务所的丽莎·卡坦（Lisa Kattan）将讲解ITP（国际贸易委员会）的导航问题，我将回顾2026年的专利案例，罗森布鲁姆（Rothwell Figg）将讨论专利申请问题。周五下午的会议可能是最值得提前规划的，Scott Alter和Jon Trembath将讨论专利复审和再审查的策略，包括如何避免加强赔偿，以及面对变化的专利审判和上诉委员会（PTAB）的情况。这一描述是外交辞令，指的是局长对立案的扩大控制权，美国专利商标局现在正在大量诉讼中维护这一权力。

**人工智能主题**
本次会议贯穿着人工智能主题。伦敦Bird & Bird律师事务所的Nick Aries和Debevoise的梅根·班尼根（Megan Bannigan）将在周四上午讲解如何保护知识产权免受人工智能系统的侵害；Debevoise的Kendall Howell将在伦理时段讨论人工智能时代的法律实践；Ann McCrackin将在周五讲解人工智能工具对知识产权律师的帮助。此外，还有商标和版权议程，包括Cobalt律师事务所的Tsan Abrahamson讨论专利商标局（PTO）和商标试验委员会（TTAB），WilmerHale的Mindy Sooter和Louis Tompros讨论版权，Debevoise的Josh Lerner讨论商业秘密，Phyllis Marcus讨论全国广告部门，Versant Media的Jeremy Kaufman讨论艺术伪造品，以及关于域名治理的小组讨论，由世界知识产权组织（WIPO）的Brian Beckham、亚马逊的Dana Brown Northcott和互联网商务协会的Zak Muscovitch参与。

报名和完整议程请访问cle.com。每年都有一些参会者从未穿过滑雪装备，但仍然度过了一段美好的时光。

我将在12月开始整理2026年的案例清单。如果您认为有任何专利判决或问题值得纳入，请告诉我。
articles.summary:
by Dennis Crouch

Time to make January plans. The IP CLE Conference returns to the Grand Hyatt Vail on January 6-9, 2027, and I will again be handling the patent case law review on Saturday morning. David Bernstein (Debevoise & Plimpton) and Scott Alter (Michael Best) co-chair the program, which is co-sponsored by the ABA Section of Intellectual Property Law. This is the ski CLE, so the schedule is built around the mountain: morning sessions run 7:00 to 9:15, the middle of the day is a “Ski Break,” and the program picks back up from 4:00 to 7:00 in the late afternoon.

I have been coming to this one for years, and what keeps me returning is the mix of people in the room and wintery mix on the mountain. Federal Circuit Judge Kara Stoll and Judge J. Campbell Barker (E.D. Tex., Tyler) close the conference Saturday afternoon in a bench-and-bar dialogue with Willy Jay, who moved his Supreme Court and appellate practice to Paul Weiss last month. Two in-house panels bookend the final days: CoorsTek, Sandisk, and Medtronic on Friday, then Dolby, Samsung, Microsoft, Pure Storage, and Intel on Saturday.

The patent block. Saturday morning is the patent-heavy stretch: Lisa Kattan (Baker Botts) on navigating the ITC, my look back at 2026, and Brian Rosenbloom (Rothwell Figg) on prosecution issues. Friday’s late-afternoon session may be the one most worth planning around. Scott Alter and Jon Trembath are covering IPR and reexamination strategy, including how to avoid enhanced damages, “in view of a fluid Patent Trial and Appeal Board.” That is a diplomatic phrase for the Director’s expanded control over institution, which the Office is now defending across a substantial volume of litigation.

AI runs through the program. Nick Aries (Bird & Bird, London) and Megan Bannigan (Debevoise) open Thursday morning on protecting IP against AI systems; Kendall Howell (Debevoise) has the ethics hour on practicing in the age of AI; and Ann McCrackin covers AI tools for the IP attorney on Friday. There is a full trademark and copyright track as well, including Tsan Abrahamson (Cobalt) on the PTO and TTAB, Mindy Sooter and Louis Tompros (WilmerHale) on copyright, Josh Lerner (Debevoise) on trade secrets, Phyllis Marcus on the National Advertising Division, Jeremy Kaufman (Versant Media) on art forgeries, and a domain-name governance panel with Brian Beckham of WIPO, Dana Brown Northcott of Amazon, and Zak Muscovitch of the Internet Commerce Association.

Registration and the full agenda are at cle.com. A good number of attendees each year never put on skis and still have a fabulous time.

I will start assembling the 2026 case list in December. If there is a patent decision or issue you think belongs – send it my way.

articles.title: It’s Down There Somewhere: Viavi’s Section 285 Fee Award Affirmed
articles.content:
by Dennis Crouch
Viavi Solutions Inc. v. Platinum Optics Technology Inc. (PTOT), No. 2025-1362 (Fed. Cir. Sept. 8, 2026) (nonprecedential)
Analogy is a key feature of judicial reasoning. Today’s decision uses The Big Lebowski to make the point that discovery cannot be used as an open-ended search for a claim that a plaintiff does not yet have. Affirming an exceptional-case finding under § 285, the Federal Circuit compared Viavi’s proposed search through PTOT’s business records to the film’s hapless intruders repeatedly dunking the Dude in a toilet while looking for money that was not there, prompting the Dude’s sarcastic response: “It’s down there somewhere, let me take another look.”
Viavi sued PTOT in the N.D. Cal. over optical filters used for 3D sensing in mobile phones, accusing a single sample filter in its possession, the "11246 Filter," "or a filter that is not materially different than that." Five months in, PTOT moved for summary judgment with a declaration stating that the 11246 Filter had not been designed for the accused devices and had not been manufactured or sold since May 2020. Viavi never contested that declaration, never deposed the declarant, and never sought discovery aimed at testing it. It also never dropped the filter from its infringement contentions, keeping it in place, as its counsel put it, as "belt and suspenders" while pursuing discovery aimed at finding some other PTOT filter to accuse instead. Viavi ultimately dismissed its case with prejudice, which mooted the summary judgment motion before it was ever decided. Judge Davila then found the case exceptional and started the fee clock on the day that declaration was filed. The Federal Circuit has now affirmed.

articles.title: CAFC Oral Args
articles.content:
法院将于周二（9月8日）上午听取四起专利上诉案。案件包括：

1. **麦金利诉Luv n' care**（案号：24-2244，25-1087，25-1109）：涉及陪审团对“一般平坦”的裁决，以及技术顾问的费用是否应作为成本纳税的问题；
2. **Traxcell Technologies诉Cellco Partnership**（案号：25-1496，25-1683）：争议焦点在于第285条费用裁定是否在实体判决下达后仍然有效；
3. **Edge Systems诉Cartessa Aesthetics**（案号：25-1119，25-1190）：考察地方法院是否可以在未对“多管”进行解释的情况下，直接做出不侵权的摘要判决；
4. **马萨诸塞大学诉Forte Biosciences**（案号：25-1342）：探讨委员会是否可以接受未符合其对技术人员定义的声明人证词。

（需登录或成为会员才能阅读完整内容）
articles.summary:
by Dennis Crouch

The Federal Circuit will hear oral arguments in four patent appeals on Tuesday morning (Sept 8).

  • McGinley v. Luv n' care (Nos. 24-2244, 25-1087, 25-1109) (a jury verdict on "generally flat," plus whether a technical advisor's fees are taxable as costs);
  • Traxcell Technologies v. Cellco Partnership (Nos. 25-1496, 25-1683) (whether a Section 285 fee award entered after the merits mandate issued is void);
  • Edge Systems v. Cartessa Aesthetics (Nos. 25-1119, 25-1190) (whether the district court could grant summary judgment of noninfringement without construing "manifold"); and
  • University of Massachusetts v. Forte Biosciences (No. 25-1342) (whether the Board could credit declarants who did not satisfy its own definition of the skilled artisan).
